agenda: Review the first-run journey for drivers joining Kestrel Dispatch on a carrier-managed phone.
Walk the new stop list and resolve what completion means when coverage disappears.
Check contrast, screen reader behavior, and the swipe-versus-button disagreement.
Agree notification wording, prototype revisions, and evidence needed before a release decision.

chapters.title: First Run and Driver Onboarding
beats: Priya frames the review around a driver starting a 24-stop shift, not a public launch decision.
Jonas shows a four-step first-run path: invite, carrier confirmation, permissions in context, and a sample stop; Mei challenges the permission order and recovery path.
Hannah flags that 'ready to drive' overpromises if location is denied, and the team chooses plain language and a saveable retry state.

chapters.title: Stop List and Offline Completion
beats: Jonas presents a stop list showing time window, address, proof requirement, and status without opening each card.
Mei distinguishes queued, accepted, and rejected actions and challenges any design that silently treats a queued completion as final.
Priya and Mei agree to keep offline completion visible as pending and preserve the driver's note during a dispatch reassignment conflict.

chapters.title: Accessible Completion Control
beats: Mei identifies contrast failures in the amber queued badge and a screen reader label that reads only 'button'.
Jonas argues swipe-to-complete reduces accidental taps on mounted phones; Mei argues an explicit confirm button works with gloves and assistive technology.
Priya leaves the control choice open for observed driver testing and requires a high-contrast, screen-reader-usable version of both alternatives.

chapters.title: Notification Copy, Owners, and Close
beats: Hannah proposes separate push messages for a route change, a queued action, and an accepted completion, without implying success before server confirmation.
Mei limits notification detail on the lock screen and requires idempotent server receipts; Jonas adds an in-app status history for uncertain connections.
The team assigns Jonas, Mei, Hannah, and Priya concrete follow-ups while keeping release scope and the swipe decision open for later planning.
